tagline.text: A red-brick church founded in 1586, with a dome and a four-story belfry

location.label: Location
location.text: In front of the plaza, beside the national highway, Santa Lucia, Ilocos Sur

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱0–500 (church visit plus nearby transport and snacks, per day)

children.text: Santa Lucia Church is a red-brick church standing on the site where Augustinian friars founded a mission in 1586. It has a dome that is rare in Ilocos Sur and a four-story belfry, and it is known for a dark-faced statue of the saint believed to cure eye ailments.

Santa Lucia Church stands beside the national highway in the town of Santa Lucia, Ilocos Sur, right in front of the town plaza. It lies between Candon City and Santa Cruz, so it is an easy stop on the road from Manila up to Vigan. Its formal name is Saint Lucy the Martyr Church, and it is also described as a diocesan shrine. The town's official website calls it one of the most beautiful churches in Ilocos Sur.
The history begins on
January 5, 1586

, when Augustinian friars established a mission here (the Ministerio de Kaog), which had earlier been attached to the mission of Candon. The present building is said to have been completed by the friars around
(one account says construction began around 1871) and renovated in

. Red brick walls, a rose window on the facade, flying buttresses on the east and west sides, and a dome said to resemble St. Peter's Basilica define its look. The claim that it is the only church in Ilocos Sur with a dome is widely repeated, but the claim that it is the only one in the whole Philippines is hard to verify. The town was once called Kaog, and during the Spanish period it was also known as Dumangague. According to local legend, when the Spaniards were treating the local people harshly, an old woman appeared, gave her name as Lucia, and vanished, and a church was then built on that spot. The town website says that the friars asked for the town to be named Santa Lucia that same year. Legend and historical record do not match, so enjoy the story as a story. The town website records that in
the monastery had two religious serving about 3,600 people, and that the town became a regular parish in

The heart of local devotion is the statue of St. Lucy. The old wooden statue is lovingly called "Apo Baket" (Grandmother), and people with eye problems pray to it for healing. Silver votive offerings shaped like eyes, arms, and legs are pinned thickly to the garments of the statue before the altar, showing how long the devotion has lasted. The saint's feast day is
December 13
every year, and pilgrims come from other areas at that time.
This is not a large tourist attraction. A visit takes
30 minutes to 1 hour

, and it works well as the first stop on an Ilocos Sur Visita Iglesia (church pilgrimage) route that continues to Candon Church, Santa Maria Church, and Vigan. This guide includes only the fares, hours, and schedules that could be confirmed, so please check the latest information before you go. The town as a whole had a population of about 26,000 in 2024 and is made up of 36 barangays, a quiet rural town that is easy and relaxed to explore on foot.

The facade combines red brick with white finishing, and a round window above the arched doors shows St. Lucy. The facade faces east, so early morning gives the best photos. Midday shadows are strong and make photography difficult.

blocks.title: A rare dome for Ilocos Sur

children.text: The dome, said to be modeled on St. Peter's Basilica, is the church's most distinctive feature. The ceiling painting is said to imitate Michelangelo's Creation of Adam. Most of the dome's stained-glass windows are said to have broken over the years.
A four-story belfry is attached to the left side of the church. It collapsed in the earthquake of
and was restored in
. A staircase to the right of the entrance is said to lead up to the belfry and a second-floor choir platform, so please check on site whether it is open.

blocks.title: Biblical ceiling paintings and arched windows

children.text: Large arched windows let natural light into the interior. The ceiling shows biblical scenes such as the Sacrifice of Isaac and the Annunciation. Some accounts also say that the four Evangelists are painted on the four columns supporting the dome over the altar.

blocks.title: Golden altar and the saint's statue

children.text: The central altar is a two-level golden retablo with St. Lucy as its centerpiece, flanked by two smaller altars. The statue, hung with silver offerings by devotees, is the main thing to see in this church. People may be praying, so please look quietly. The old wooden statue has a face darkened by age, glass eyes, and a wig of human hair, and for that reason it is also called the "Dark Virgin." Devotees are said to rub the silver offerings on their eyes while praying for healing.

blocks.title: The convent that served as a Katipunan headquarters

children.text: A large convent stands northwest of the church. During the revolution it is said to have served as the headquarters of Katipunan forces led by General Manuel Tinio. Later a congregation of sisters used it, and it was severely damaged in the 1990 earthquake. Whether the interior is open to visitors is not known. Seeing it together with the church helps you sense that this town was once a place where history happened.

Peanuts are the local specialty, and Santa Lucia is nicknamed the "Peanut Capital of Ilocos Sur." A One-Town-One-Product (OTOP) center along the highway is said to sell peanut products. It is a good place to pick up snacks after visiting the church. In May 2024 the first Rambak Mani Festival was held to promote the peanut industry. The town also has People's Park, the old municipal hall building, and some old ancestral houses, which make for an easy walk after the church.

items.title: 1–2 hour route
items.subtitle: A walk around the church and town plaza

children.text: Arrive when the light reaches the east-facing facade, and photograph the brickwork, the rose window, and the belfry.
Go inside and take your time with the ceiling paintings, the dome, the central altar, and the saint's statue. If Mass is in progress, look around quietly from the back.
Walk past the convent beside the church, the plaza, and the municipal hall across the road to get a feel for the town.
Stop at a peanut shop along the highway for snacks, then move on to your next destination.
The exact Mass times could not be confirmed for this guide. If you want to visit during Mass, ask the local parish.
If you are coming up from the south, make Santa Lucia Church your first stop.
Head north to Candon City and visit Candon Church.
Have lunch in Candon or Vigan, then go on to Santa Maria Church (World Heritage Site).
Arrive in Vigan and stay overnight to walk the historic city.
Travel times between stops vary greatly with traffic, so please check locally.
Santa Lucia is about
from Manila. The most common way to get there is a long-distance bus from Manila bound for Vigan or Laoag.

Take a Vigan-bound bus and tell the staff to let you off at Santa Lucia. Viron Transit lists Santa Lucia as a stop on its Ilocos Sur fare table from Manila (Cubao and Dapitan terminals; ₱726 one way, undated, so confirm the current fare), and one visitor account presents Santa Lucia as the first stop for travelers coming up from Manila. Buses of other companies may only go as far as Candon or Vigan, so ask whether they stop here before boarding.
Bus companies, fares, and travel times change from season to season, so confirm them with the terminal or the company before you leave.
The church is right beside the national highway, so it is easy to find once you get off.
Santa Lucia is about
70km
south of Vigan. You can go by a Manila-bound bus or by van.
Candon City is the neighboring town to the north and Santa Cruz is the neighboring town to the south.
The nearest airport is Laoag International Airport. There are flights from Manila to Laoag. Check the schedule with the airline.
If you drive or rent a car, a navigation app helps, and the church is in front of the plaza beside the highway.
The church is in front of the plaza in the town center, so most of it can be seen on foot.
For nearby towns, use buses, jeepneys, or tricycles. Check fares locally.
Since the visit is mostly indoors, weather is less of a concern. Even so, the Ilocos region is easier to travel in the dry season, and outdoor photos come out better then.

Around the saint's feast day on December 13, pilgrims increase and the atmosphere is lively. During Holy Week the church may be crowded with people doing Visita Iglesia, so choose early morning or a weekday if you want to avoid that period.

Santa Lucia is a small town, so there are not many choices for lodging and restaurants. Most travelers stay in Vigan or Candon and drop by during the day. The town website has sections for hotels and places to eat, but the details could not be confirmed.

For food, we recommend the town's specialty, peanut products. In neighboring cities you can also try salty Ilocano dishes and rice sweets, so check locally. One visitor account mentions the kalamay (sticky rice sweet) of a neighboring city.

Across from the church is the municipal hall, and markets and small shops line the highway. The town's public market is said to have opened in May 2010. Grab a quick bite here, and have a proper meal in neighboring Candon or in Vigan, which is more convenient.
The facade faces east, so early morning gives the best photos. Shadows are strong at midday.
The interior is fairly dark, and the ceiling paintings and altar are much easier to see when the lights are on. Ask permission locally before using a tripod.
During Mass, avoid flash and loud talking, and do not disturb people who are praying.
A visit takes only 30 minutes to 1 hour, so it fits easily into a Candon, Santa Maria, and Vigan itinerary.
If you are coming up from the south, it is natural to make Santa Lucia your first stop and then head north.
Dress modestly, with shoulders and knees covered.
Access to the belfry stairs and the convent interior may change, so ask permission in person.
Mass times, donations, and feast day events can change, so check the latest announcements.
Around the saint's feast day, a procession or pilgrimage events may take place. Check the schedule with the parish or town announcements.
This is still a working parish church. During Mass and prayer, worship comes before sightseeing.
Mass schedules and opening hours could not be confirmed for this guide. Check locally.
The statue is something the faithful hold dear. Do not touch it or pose for playful photos with it.
Sources differ on the dome's uniqueness and on when the statue arrived. Treat guide texts as a reference rather than taking them at face value.
The highway is right beside the church and vehicles pass quickly. Be careful when crossing the road.
Tell the driver or conductor in advance where you want to get off the bus.
A UNESCO World Heritage Baroque church. You can reach it by traveling toward Vigan. Check travel times locally.
A UNESCO World Heritage city with a preserved Spanish colonial layout. It is about
70km
from Santa Lucia, which makes it a good base for overnight stays.
The St. John of Sahagun church in Candon City, north of Santa Lucia. It is the next stop on the Visita Iglesia route.
The municipal hall is across from the church, and the plaza continues beyond it. Sights in town, such as People's Park, are described as walkable.
